question: Does group-aware post-processing improve held-out correctness probabilities beyond score-only calibration, and does this translate into better selective acceptance?
primary_comparison: multicalibration minus Platt, paired test Brier score
selection_metric: validation Brier score; ties prefer fewer patches
candidate_policy: All ten recorded candidates, equally weighted within task. No best-of-ten selection. Alternate candidate j is paired with primary candidate j; index pairing is arbitrary, not a repair workflow.
split_policy: Preserve official validation and test partitions. Hash-sort official training task IDs, using the first 60% for base training and the rest for calibration. Never split sibling completions.
label: Publisher-provided is_correct from benchmark tests; not independently rerun and not a proof of semantic correctness.
feature_policy: Only prompt, generated program, and sampled-token log probabilities. No outcomes, difficulty annotations, task IDs, alternate-model features, or other candidate outcomes enter the confidence predictor.
cost_policy: User-selected relative cost scenario only. No measured dollars, latency, or Cursor deployment data.
scope: Independent offline replication and routing extension using public research data. No claim of a novel multicalibration algorithm, Cursor affiliation, or production validation. Protocol saved before this pipeline's test evaluation; not externally preregistered.
